question: What is the product of the reaction when anhydrite undergoes hydration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gypsum.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anhydrite** is a mineral that has the chemical formula** CaSO₄.**
 
• It is an** anhydrous form** of gypsum.
 
• When anhydrite undergoes **hydration**, it reacts with water to form gypsum (CaSO₄.2H₂O).
 
• Therefore, the product of the reaction when **anhydrite undergoes** hydration is gypsum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum **is a **soft sulfate mineral** that is widely used in construction as a building material.

 
 
• It is also used in **agriculture, medicine, and other industries.**
 
 
 
• **Limonite** is a type of** iron ore** that is **brownish-yellow** in color.
 
 
• It can precipitate from surface or groundwater that is rich in iron, and it forms from the **weathering **of other iron minerals.
 
 
 
• **Magnesite** is a mineral that has the chemical formula **MgCO₃**.
 
 
• The mineral was created either by the action of magnesium-containing solutions on** calcite **or as an alteration product from rocks rich in magnesium.
 
 
 
• **Kaolin** is a type of clay mineral that is used in **ceramics, paper,** and other industries.
 
 
• The fine particle size, plate-like or **lamellar particle shape**, and chemical inertness of hydrous kaolin are its distinguishing features.
